title: How to Look for Bird Poop
hook: Salt on a buoy casing is sometimes a better guide than another confident map.
counterintuition: Weak prediction does not require stillness. Send small probes, read traces, and let contact with reality teach before commitment grows.
tryThisNow: Run one tiny probe today that can teach you something without requiring a big prediction first.
keyTakeaway: Replace far-seeing claims with small exposures that let reality reveal useful traces.

implementationPlan.title: Replace Farseeing Claims With Small
implementationPlan.coreSkill: Train yourself to probe opaque domains instead of overselling panoramic visibility. Practice it by naming what the visible evidence can and cannot prove.

ifThenPlans.plan: If the plan feels too polished, then ask what real-world test could challenge it quickly.
If the theory seems settled, then look for a trace that could correct your confidence.
If you feel tempted to forecast your life too cleanly, then widen contact with possible paths.
If a choice starts leaning on bird poop, then write the missing pressure beside it before approving the next step.
